item.title: Sticks and Stones
item.description:
I wield my weapons like my words
As sharp as scalpel’s edge
For when I speak or write or think
I have no fear of hedge.
People seem to think that there’s
No skill in language gained
That since you speak and write and think
No growth can be exchanged.
For when you write or read so well
It’s awe that you might hear
For folks don’t seem to grasp the truth
Of learning without fear.
For just as iron horses ride by complex gears and heat
So too to wield your tongue like knives is its own grand feat.

item.title: The Body of an American / Death Wish
item.description:
Lord I pray that when I die
It’s peaceful as it goes
That I should leave sans pain or hurt
And cast off earthly woes
My mother’s father’s wake was short
and but few did appear
But more akin to Psyche than
Calypso were their tears.
No Faunus at the casket’s close
No wine or toasts were raised
No comfort found in jubilee
but relief in Charon’s shade.
When comes my turn to cross the Styx and leave these banks behind
Let those who weep weep not with joy nor remember me unkind.

item.title: Untitled Lois Lane
item.description:
“Christ, Clark,” Lois says,
She’s holding her head in her hands
She’s watching the news unsurprised
Rage in her tears and her eyes
The wine glass half empty, the notebook untouched
None of her words seem to matter enough.

Jimmy is boots on the ground
Lois is grounded for fear of the sound
Of her voice and she’s home and she’s sick
Watching the news unable to flick
Away from the channels
With smoke in the air
She closes her eyes and sends up a prayer

item.title: The Riptide
item.description:
I can’t remember learning to swim.

This, of course, is unsurprising, given my upbringing. The Second Sea was but a stone’s throw away from the outermost walls of my mother’s castle. I grew my days with fishermen’s children, swimming and harpooning and getting sucked out to sea by the currents.

I was six years old when the first riptide took me.

I was a strong swimmer, even then, but being so young, I panicked, suddenly forgetting the words that had been hammered into me since I was old enough to walk. “If a current takes you, swim in tandem with the shore.” How many had said this to me? My father, my mother, my brother, the fishermen at the dock who feared what would happen if their liege lady’s daughter drowned on their watch.

item.title: The Sonnets of Keris
item.description:
Keris is a poet. He is well known for his role in the folktale Alisandre of the Lake, with whom he was in love with. Keris, Alisandre, and Corrinthia of the Bears were deeply embroiled in each other’s lives, living together as lovers. Below is a ballad describing a version of the tale.

Keris’ Sonnets (or Kerisian Sonnets, as they are known) are comprised of three quatrains followed by a couplet. The four lines of the quatrain alternate iambic tetrameter and iambic trimeter, respectively. The couplet is a fourteener (iambic heptameter). The rhyme scheme is ABAB CDCD EFEF GG.

item.title: American Infancia
item.description:
American Infancia
July 12th, 2024
I grew up wooded and blooded by the evergreens and black crows.

American Espina
August 8th, 2025
I cut my teeth and ankles on blackberry vines and the thick green woods.

American Fair Folk
October 22nd, 2024

That’s where the faeries live; under the gray green of rotting old porches.

Double American Death Wish
June 21st, 2024
I pray when Death comes for me I jump into that final abyss like I jumped off the boathouse that summer: with a shriek, a laugh, and a splash.

item.description:
Notes: These are American Sentences written while in Ireland in September 2024. I write American Sentences wherever I go.

item.title: First Steps
item.description: Notes: These are collections of American Sentences that I have written over the years. This includes my own travel throughout the American Continent and my travel abroad. American sentences don’t have to be about America, I just happen to think about America a lot. American Sentences are a type of form poetry developed by Allen Ginsburg. Like a Haiku, they contain seventeen syllables. Unlike a Haiku, this form (ostensibly) better fits the abilities of the English Language. I’ve been writing these types of poems since I was fifteen or sixteen years old. I think because they are so small they must take a lot of practice to master. I think I still have a long way to go before I could even begin to consider myself a master of this form.

item.title: About
item.description:
The name’s Goos. Helena Goos.

A twenty-three year old from Seattle, Washington, Goos was published at the age of fifteen through Seattle Arts and Lectures. Of course, she got it into her head that she could be a writer. So here she is, regretting not double-majoring in Comp-Sci, publishing and building her own portfolio, looking for a job.

item.title: Faith Sonnet
item.description:
Faith is like a mustard seed
I’s told when I was young.
The older I have weatherd
the truer it’s become.
I miss the days when Faith and time
were blossoming and free
When I would run and play and pray
whene’er it pleaséd me.
For now my time is not my own
and neither is my faith
And I will work for forty years
before it is replaced.
I hope and pray that future times will like the mustard seed
Burst forth from hardship, toil, and pain and make just like a
tree.

I Am Ready to Put on a Show

It’s the grand finale!

item.title: Nostalgia of Days
item.description:
Where my father’s from it’s harvest time
The orchards rich with bounties fine

And the days are getting shorter
But I’m still getting older.

Where my mother’s from it’s raining steady
The humid heat hangs thick and heavy

And the days are getting shorter
But I’m still getting older.

Where I am from it’s turning sweet
the leaves are falling from the trees

And the days are getting shorter
But I’m still getting older.

item.title: Hello World
item.description:
You Can Teach An Old Dog New Tricks

Yes! It is possible to teach and old dog new tricks!

item.title: Scarlet Letters
item.description:
Unfast your heart unto the Lord
and of your sins be cleansed
For all the bile that it spews
what plagues the soul of men
I shall not turn to wickedness
in valley dark and deep
The rod and staff my Shepherd holds
will keep me like a sheep.
But Oh! Her body close to mine
the pleasures of her flesh
Her sweat so sweet and folds so soft
is where I taste her best!
My Lord is God! And holy he is mightiest on high!
Protect me will his sacred word from evil urge despised!

item.title: Mummification at Constantinople
item.description:
The voice that lives inside my head
is kindest least to me
Of sorts inverted Nightingale
she leaves me there to bleed
So weak I lie in gules smeared
by self-inflicted blow
I beg her please to stitch me up
and staunch the bitter flow
Or if she won’t apply to me
triage for soldier-downed
Then may she give me final rites
and put me in the ground
Much rather I my brains and lungs all stuffed inside a jar,
Then let her venom patch me wrong and leave another scar.

item.title: No Secrets
item.description:
(A Tragedy of my Own Design)

I say that I’m an open book
No secrets dark have I,
I haven’t got a poker face
And neither do I try.
I’ve learned there’s beauty in the depths
of every person’s mind
And delving in unfath’mable wit
more treasures do I find.
“Fool me once or fool me twice live
to fight another day,
Your faith in people’s long misplaced,”
I often hear them say,
“To wear your heart upon your sleeve will give you naught but grief.”
But even then when pierced my heart I find I still believe.

item.title: Cocaine Jesus
item.description:
See the destitute Emmanuel
on the street corner

His mind tricked out
In a consecrated communion of fentanyl and hard liquor

Transmogrified;
He sees the shape of things

His concrete garden of Gethsemane
Rises up to skin his knees
He leans further and further to rest
under the shade of an Olive Street

He preaches to the masses
Parables of blind men and public transit
Parables of trans prodigal sons and gang violence.

item.title: The Veritas Symphony (Speak Truth to All Things)
item.description:
Mvmnt. I.

And the people living in the darkness
Have seen a great light.

And he said unto me:
Vertiatem dīc omnibus.

And he said unto us:
Vertiatem dīc omnibus.

My fellow velites
My contubernium of Christ

Did they hear this plea upon the cross?

This fire that burns in me
The same that made Moses holy

Will I, the eagle, immolate?

Mvmnt. II.

When I was young I knew of a boy
Who burned with fever day and night
“That’s spiritual war,” they said.

item.title: Heliophile
item.description:
I feel each pulse inside me,
a drawing towards the light,
And steady goes my beating heart
Since end of longest night.
Each day is like a blessing
The twilight lingers just
A little more with passing days;
I revel in the dusk.
My mind has been aflame with words
And fervent they doth pour
Out of my mouth onto the page
Since winters’ losing score.
And so I write with cogent blaze and trail the sun in kind,
God, I think, it’s such a gift to even be alive.

item.title: A Poker Game with the Anemoi
item.description:
At card games I have never been
a deft or winning hand
I lack the military mind
that’s built for cards and land.
But still I fumble through the play
for neither Spring nor Fall
Nor Summer have a better mind
to win from me at all.
But Winter she’s a tactful match
and always calls my bluff
And steals my winnings like a sponge
of darker matter stuff.
But as the days go on and on, the winner’s hand goes slack
And bit by bit come longest night my daylight I win back.

item.title: I Hear Them All
item.description: Notes: Inspired by the song, “I Hear Them All” by Old Crow Medicine Show. Check it out here.

item.title: Winter Folio, Sonnet 17
item.description:
The lake is like a looking glass
a silver pane of gray
She casts the vis’ge of the sky
back into the fray.
No gentle ripple o’re her face
serene and still she stays
I scry into her frigid depths
in search of warmer days.
And then I find in gelid plunge
my breath is borne away
But lo! a light above me shines
the promise of gold rays.
But when the surface parts for me and I draw in light wind
I find the sun was born a dream of winter gloom again.

item.title: The Kiss; the Knife
item.description:
And Brutus,

Like Judas

Betrays his

Savior. The

man who gave

him every-

thing. The man

like family.

And Brutus

Like Judas

Wept to see

His brother

Dead.

item.title: SPQA
item.description:
Notes: The hero image for this post was generated by ChatGPT. I do not own this image.


And the prophets communing with God,
Descend the mountain top

Scream and shout til’ their voices are raw
In the seizing of the day

They break down the doors of the Senate
Demanding more

Bull’s horns distinguish the velites
From the legionary

Stars and bars
red and gold
the banners wave

The eagle, immortalized
In white and blue
In red and gold

item.title: Ave Maria
item.description:
Hard pressed am I
By god and holy fire
To think of the Vestal Virgin Mary

Holy she upon the back of a donkey
Pursued by the wolves of Italy
And the serpent of her own people

Her husband, looks upon her with worry
Eyes that see his son clutched tight
In the arms of his beloved wife

And in dead of night they flee
Gifts of gold and frankincense and myrrh
Cover them, the Life of the World
Interred in death’s scents

item.title: Martha's Sonnet
item.description:
The party will be soon and there
is still much to be done
The bread is nearly ready and
the chicken’s underdone.
I need to whip the cream and crush
the chickpeas for the stew
My sister is but little help
she sits there next to you.
She hangs on to your every word
while the lamb is burning
And Jesus Christ I need some help
the latkes need a’turning.
You look at me with gentle eyes and laughter in your smile,
“Martha, come and take a break, just for a little while.”

item.title: The Obedient Son
item.description:
And so I stayed and off you went
with your inheritance
Seeking out a newer high—
a better life than this.
As if the tending of the fields
and keeping of the house
Was far beneath your softened hands
and perfectly coifed crown.
And so I stayed and kept the fields
and counted up the grain
I helped our father up the stairs
and served him when in pain.
And here you come and father says that I too should rejoice,
But I will not—I stayed and served when faced with easier choice.

item.title: Cain's Sonnet
item.description:
Hey, it’s nice to meet you I’m your
older brother now
Your face is sweet as honeycomb
your hair like feathered down.
Oh baby brother I can’t wait
to teach you all I know
We’ll play at knights and dragons
and tussle in the snow.
I’ll show you all the bugs and things
that wriggle on the ground
We’ll unearth logs and stones and rocks
and run through muddy grounds.
O baby brother I will be the lion to your lamb,
I’ll keep you safe, I’ll watch your back, I’ll do the best I can.

item.title: Summer Folio, Sonnet 13
item.description:
(Commonly known as the Music Sonnet)

When first I came unto this land
across the stormy sea
I brought my binjar and my songs
and all my harmonies.
I wandered long, a troubadour,
in search of newer sound
And in this land so large and vast
a freshness did abound.
And lo! It had me in a hold
of scales and notes so fine,
I could not help but copy-straight
so I could make it mine.
And so I pluck my strings with care and hope that you will hear
The echoes of my homeland and the love that I found here.

item.title: Winter Folio, Sonnet 9
item.description:
The winter hath not come to pass
and fall it clings to breath,
But here the sun has gone away
and I go to my depths.
The leaves they shiver from their trees
the ground it stirs first frost
The lake begins its frigid plunge
into complete warmth lost.
The birds they sing not in the morn
for even they too know
That soon will come the constant gray
and mounds of pillowed snow.
And in the mornings when I rise, I cast my quilts away,
But sleep it lingers like the clouds and beds me down in day.

item.title: Untitled Lake Sonnet / Gray Matter Sonnet
item.description:
The brume and mist they hang about
My lake and frontal lobe
The sun it breaks through far too late
To brighten my abode.
Tempestuous, the clouds droop low
and lap up at the waves
Amygdala, like cloud-stirred lake
Refuses to behave.
Hippocampus, she rebels
And she unlike the lake
Has no reason to upheave
Like wind or snow or slake.
And though I have all everything that anyone could want
I find my mind is like the lake in deep gray winter months.

item.title: My Lady of the Lake --- Ode of the 520
item.description:
The Ocean is a fickle Love
of salt and wind and brine
But she is next to nothing here
against this mistress mine.
My Lady she is of the lake
and mist and rain and fog
She one moment to the next
is sullen, angry, calm.
She blows no storms nor winds of strength
nor brings torrential rains
But batter she this concrete bridge
on which my love sustains.
My Lady Lake I fear her not on days when it is clear
But when she rages capped in white I know not to draw near.

item.title: Sonnet for Fall Insomnia
item.description:
I find these days of autumn chill
Straight cut me to the core
My sleepless mind it drifts and drafts
From couch to chair and floor.
I think sometimes that I’m at fault
For mind-fog weary ways
And for the time and space I spend
Lost in a sleepy haze.
But still the seasons change and turn
The planet she spins on
And as the sunlight fades away
My smile goes along.
So early sleep is how I try to put myself at ease
But even then I wake to find the rest is little peace.

item.title: Sonnet for the Coming Winter
item.description:
The winter in my city comes
Close on the heels of fall
A sudden leap from gold and leaf,
Into a great gray maw.
And so one day you wake to find
Your own sun you must make
And azure light becomes your ward
To keep the storm at bay.
But as the winter waxes long
The storm it gathers clouds,
The reaches of my thalamus
become a battleground.
And come the months of constant gray I toss and turn in bed,
For there is precious little sun to soothe my stormy head.

item.title: The Sisters
item.description:
The mountains in a distant haze
the gentle sun above
The sky so blue it goes for days,
like hearts in youthful love.
The orchards in their verdant rows,
The green that springs from ground,
The smell of rain and blossoms sweet,
around me do compound.
Oh spring is such a quiet song,
the birds are in the trees,
And summer comes in baritone,
In heat and harmony.
The summer is my favorite love since she is warm and clean,
But come she can only if preceded by the spring.

item.title: The Sun
item.description:
The sun! The sun! She’s come again,
The cry goes in my mind,
Across my cells both cheers and shouts
And dopamine collide.
Oh gracious she, that yellow thing,
Suspended in the sky,
She smiles as I smile back,
She graces me from high.
The gentle sun whispers such sweet
Sweet nothings in my ear,
She chases back my nimbus dark,
And dissipates my fear.
So in this land of seldom sun, her halo I drink in,
For when the seasons turn to grey, I’ll see her little then.

item.title: Castle Caldera or The Watersnake and the Reed Grass
Water in the Desert or Why the Laughing Dog Laughs
item.description:
The carrion birds were circling as Marie struggled to walk upright in the loose sand.

Far on the northstearn horizon, a hazy shadow in the distance, the Lontaigne Mountains loomed. She glanced at the birds above. They think me a meal already. They will be disappointed. She knew that this line of thinking was futile, but it was all she had.

Her water had run out a day ago. A day? Perhaps it had been two. She no longer could conceptualize time under the scorching heat of the Western sun.

item.title: Summer Folio, Sonnet 1
item.description:
We quarrel oft the Bear and I
she hates my wit and writ,
But she is stubborn as a dog
and I will not submit.
I match the Bear both tooth and claw,
(which she hates the most)
Each parry, jab, and spited word,
I give not ground or post.
The Bear is often in my thoughts
and sometimes in my dreams,
She tracks me down with utmost skill
and then does as she pleases.
The Bear she says she loves you best, but I think this a lie,
I see the way she looks at me and thinks that she is sly.

item.title: The Deep; it Beckons
item.description:
The beach glows tonight. It’s a soft glow, a murmuration of light.

It’s not anything spectacular, but everything has that moonshine sheen to it. The moon hangs there in the sky, a quarter past her zenith, like some silver-glass fishing float adrift in a midnight sea.

item.title: Autumn Folio, Sonnet 10
item.description:
You stare into the distance love,
(I wish to see your mind)
I see that when you look at me
you look with empty eyes.
You haven’t left your vigil love,
beside the tower’s port,
You look to where your family lies,
towards your father’s court.
Love come in, you’ll catch your death,
I say, and draw you in,
But worthless are my soothing words
to reach your walls within.
I hear your sobs on quiet nights, when you should be asleep,
I try to steal away your frown, but you do naught but weep.

item.title: Winter Folio, Sonnet 1
item.description:
(Commonly known as Keris’ Grief Begins)
In azure vault my lady lies,
(she thinks I do not know)
She hangs suspended like a cloud,
in a frigid sky below.
If like a stage-hand I could draw
that fractal glass aback,
I would soon soar in frozen sky
and win my lady back.
See her dance among the stars
of winter there below?
She like a falcon dips and weaves,
among celestial snow.
But hollow ice and hollow hearts with weight begin to crack,
And in this hollow chamber here, I know she shan’t come back.

item.title: Crisis of Faith
item.description:
Notes: Another experiment in repeat panels, specifically focusing on using repeat panels to create space between each line of dialogue or moment. Coloring and lighting practice here as well.
There is certainly a way to condense this script so that it’s shorter and makes more efficient use of space. However, want to acknowledge that in a shorter script the writer has more control over the panel structure. In a 6+ issue run it’s tedious and inefficient for the writer to try and retain full control over every single panel and every single page.

item.description:
Notes: The purpose of this story is to practice comic script formatting and the re-use of panel structures in order to streamline personal comic process. Additionally, since I am a poor colorist, this comic will make use of the gray scale and contrast in order to convey depth and distinction.
You can find the comic here.

item.title: Plastic, Bone, Bisque
item.description:
A note for those not familiar with clay:
*Clay can be virtually recycled throughout its lifetime in a studio, up until the point where it goes through its first firing in a kiln. Clay goes through three stages in studio: plastic (at its softest and most pliable), leather hard (still pliable but much stiffer and harder to work with), and bone-dry (virtually all the water inside the clay has evaporated and you are left with a rather fragile, brittle material).

item.title: And They Do
item.description:
The silence stretches,
yawning across the land.
Quiet, so quiet.
A strange reverie, unbroken by sound.
The bombs have stopped.
The children, born in a world where
the thunder is a part of life,
whimper.
The elders,
so few,
so old,
raise their heads in disbelief.
For they remember,
a time when bombs did not fall,
when the earth did not shake,
when birds sang and life went on,
undisturbed by the screams of fighter jets and families.

item.title: Inexhaustible Abundance
item.description: Sarah walked across the barren earthscape, oxygen mask covering her face, goggles fogging as she exhaled. It was spring, (according to the calendar in the bunker) but the sky was still choked with the dust and smog of everything. Watery sun filtered through the particulates, illuminating the landscape in a cream-colored light.

item.title: Compass that Points Her Home
item.description:
My mother is Korean,
from a small fishing village (not so small now), in South Korea.
It’s called 퍼 항,

Pohang

She came to America,
Six years old,
Wide eyed,
Youngest of five.
She couldn’t speak any English that first year.
Now, 43 years later,
Korean is barely an echo on her tongue.
I beg her to teach me 한글,

Hangul

To teach me the heartbeat tongue of Korean;
But she knows only enough to speak with 할 머 기,
